collection.credit:
CHATGPT-WRITTEN EVENTS — WITH LORSIEAB2 CREATIVE DIRECTION
* V6–V8 additional VV1–VV5 event prose, variants and codas:
  ChatGPT, with Lorsieab2's canon guidance, character preferences,
  requests for emotional complexity and patcher constraints.

ledger.why: implementation note: no housing change is made (the games have no housing effect)

intro.name: Tight quarters
intro.text:
The village has welcomed several newcomers, but sleeping space is tight. A family with a nursing infant needs a quiet place to rest, an elder prefers to remain near familiar neighbors, and two energetic apprentices have somehow accumulated enough tools to fill an entire hut.
(Builder) has drawn a plan. (Elder) dislikes it. (Apprentice) claims that (apprentice.his/her) tools need "room to breathe." {@Chief} asks everyone to come to an agreement before nightfall.

text_only.reason: dislikes a plan, not a game preference

choices.label: Arrange huts around accessibility and daily needs.
Build or repair more space as soon as possible.
Let the affected villagers negotiate their own arrangement.

f1.text: A quiet corner is reserved for the nursing parent and infant. The apprentices move their tools elsewhere.

f2.text: A family offers to share a larger hut with the newcomers. Everyone agrees on privacy and sleeping arrangements.

f3.text: The plan keeps families together but leaves an elder too far from (elder.his/her) usual support. {@Chief} requests revisions.

n1.text: The elder is placed near the hospital and familiar neighbors; the family receives a quieter space.

n2.text: A builder notices that one path becomes slippery after rain. The village changes the proposed arrangement.

n3.text: The villagers discover that the apparently smallest hut has the best ventilation. They reconsider their assumptions.

n4.text: A villager asks whether anyone has actually spoken to the people being moved. {@Chief} pauses the meeting to ask.

m1.text: Skilled builders repair an unused shelter in time.

text_only.reason: rule 8: the event builds no structure; the repair is told

m2.text: The project takes longer than expected. The villagers agree on a temporary arrangement without separating the infant from the nursing parent.

m3.text: The apprentices volunteer to build extra storage for their tools. The elder remarks that this is their first good idea.

m4.text: A new doorway is installed backward. The builders fix it before anyone moves in.

t1.text: Everyone listens, and the villagers find a compromise that {@chief} had not considered.

t2.text: The apprentices agree to share a workshop instead of storing tools where people sleep.

t3.text: The elder reveals that (elder.he/she) does not mind moving, provided (elder.his/her) favorite chair comes too.

t4.text: The discussion becomes an argument over who snores the loudest. {@Chief} insists this is not a contest.

e1.text: By evening, everyone has a safe place to rest. The village feels a little more like home.

e2.text: {@Chief} asks the builders to write down what they learned before the next group of newcomers arrives.

e3.text: A father thanks the villagers for asking what his family actually needed instead of making assumptions.

e4.text: The apprentices' tools are finally organized. One immediately loses a hammer.

e5.text: The elder invites the newcomers for tea and complains about the village's architecture with great affection.
